graph.title: LED Bar Graph
notes: Step 1 parts were correct; no parts added or dropped.
The image shows 10 discrete red LEDs, each in series with a 220 ohm resistor, so no LED bar graph part is used.

Each LED's anode shares a breadboard column with its resistor. The resistor straddles the centre gap, and the Arduino signal wire plugs into the same column on the other half, so each pin drives anode through the resistor. LED cathodes go to the negative power rail, which is wired to Arduino GND.

Breadboard hole names follow the catalogue convention (bank 't' = rows a-e, bank 'b' = rows f-j). The image labels rows in the opposite orientation, so the exact row letters are my best mapping. Column numbers come from the image.
LED k uses Arduino pin 12-k (pin 11 for LED 1 through pin 2 for LED 10), in columns 4, 6, ..., 22.

The potentiometer sits in columns 27-29 across the centre gap: GND in column 27, wiper (SIG) in column 28 on the other half, VCC in column 29. 5V goes to column 29, A0 to column 28, and GND from the negative rail to column 27.
The top power rail is treated as one continuous negative strip (tn), though the image shows a visual gap in its middle. The Arduino GND used is GND.1, the header pin next to pin 13.
